newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH SECRET SERVICE TARGETS BUSINESS, DRUG CRIME.
newsitem.headline: POLISH SECRET SERVICE TARGETS BUSINESS, DRUG CRIME.

text.p: Poland's State Protection Office (UOP), the security service, is focusing efforts on business and drug-related crime, noting its sharp rise, UOP said in a report on Wednesday.
UOP said the number of investigations in business-related crime was already at 97 cases in June this year against 111 in the whole of last year.
"This type of crime is especially worrisome because it can have negative effects on the whole economy," the UOP statement released at a news conference said.
The report said business-related crime in most cases concerned cheating to obtain bank credit, credit guarantees and issuing shares or bonds without fulfilling the necessary legal requirements.
The report also said some government officials did not properly supervise public orders and tenders, firms evaded taxes and managers acted for personal profit.
The report said business-related crime caused estimated losses of 158 million zlotys plus another $24 million in 1996.
UOP -- which probes only crime posing a potential threat to national security -- investigated 72 drug-related criminal cases in the first half of this year compared with 58 cases in the whole 1996.

"The amount of drugs passing through our country indicates Poland's role as a transit country is growing....We estimate that 35 percent of all drugs reaching western Europe comes via Poland," the report said.
It said Poland specialised in producing high grade amphetamines which are smuggled to the Nordic countries, Germany and Holland. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
